decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Save a bookmark (P1) — paste a link, it's stored with a title.' R1 client: 'The proposed scope and priorities work for me... I approve it.' Confirmed R4 'routes/bookmarks.js — create'.
decisions.note: Spec-gate decision; save-by-URL conforms to reference. Client gave bare approval.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Browse... see your list newest-first... click to open the page.' R4 maker: 'add form, live search, tag filter, open-in-new-tab'. R1 client bare approval.
decisions.note: List view exposing items and open-original-url conform to reference. Conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker (spec gate): 'Auto-fetch page titles best-effort; fall back to the URL.' R4 maker: 'title.js — best-effort <title> fetch with URL fallback'. R1 client: 'The proposed scope and priorities work for me; I approve it.'
decisions.note: REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title, description, favicon, AND preview image; the maker affirmatively presented title-only. REF-BM-03 (editing an auto-collected description) is consequently unfulfilled. Client gave bare approval and never expressed the missing metadata expectation. Prototype/spec review stage.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'see your list newest-first'. R3 maker task table: US2 'Search, newest-first, open-in-new-tab'. No user-selectable sort key ever presented. R1/R3 client bare approvals ('scope and priorities work for me'; 'Yes, please proceed').
decisions.note: REF-BM-22 requires sorting by a chosen key (date added, title, etc.); maker fixed a single newest-first ordering. Affirmative narrowed presentation, so divergence established. Client never surfaced a sort-choice expectation.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'search by keyword'. R3 maker: US2 'Search'. R4 maker: 'live search'. No #tag syntax, boolean/parenthesised operators, or quoted-phrase exact match presented anywhere. R1 client bare approval.
decisions.note: Maker presented plain keyword search, a narrower fulfilment than reference's #tag search (14), AND/OR/NOT + groups (15), and quoted-phrase exact match (16). Divergence established from the narrowed presentation; client expressed no expectation for advanced search operators.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'add tags and notes, filter by tag'. R4 maker: 'add form, live search, tag filter'. R1 client bare approval.
decisions.note: Assigning tags and filtering by a tag conform to reference. (REF-BM-10 tag autocomplete was never presented — treated as an unpresented omission, not counted as a confirmed divergence per the missing-evidence rule.)

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'add tags and notes'; slice 3 'Organize & annotate'. R4 maker: 'long-note truncation' (plain-text note handling; no markdown rendering mentioned). R1 client bare approval; R4 client 'I can save, find, organize...' with no note-formatting expectation.
decisions.note: REF-BM-23 requires markdown notes rendered on view; maker presented plain notes only (a functional difference, not an equivalent implementation). Borderline but established as narrowed. Unexpressed by client.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Edit & delete (P3) — fix titles, update tags'. R4 maker: 'update' endpoint + 'edit dialog'. R1 client bare approval.
decisions.note: Editing a bookmark's fields conforms to reference. Conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'remove items (with a confirm step)'. R4 maker: 'delete-with-confirmation'. R1 client bare approval.
decisions.note: Delete a bookmark conforms to reference. Conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker (plan gate): 'Duplicate detection compares a normalized form of the URL, so trivial variants... don't sneak in as duplicates.' R4 maker: 'saving the same address twice is warned rather than silently duplicated' (409 path). R2 client: 'The plan looks right.'
decisions.note: Normalized-URL dedupe that warns/prevents a duplicate realises REF-BM-06's core convergence-to-existing intent; treated as conforming (functionally equivalent). Note the presentation is a warning rather than an explicit 'open existing to edit' flow — borderline but not counted as a divergence.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker (spec gate): 'Out of scope for v1: importing browser bookmarks, sharing with others, saving non-web resources.' R1 client: 'The proposed scope and priorities work for me... I approve it.'
decisions.note: REF-BM-30 (import bookmarks in Netscape HTML) was affirmatively excluded by the maker. Explicit-exclusion presentation establishes divergence. Client approved the scope wholesale without expressing an import expectation, so unexpressed. (Export REF-BM-31 was never mentioned — unpresented omission, not counted.)

decision.evidence: R1 maker offered 'Question 1: Access model (single-user vs. multi-user)'. R1 client: 'Q1: A — single-user, no login.'
decision.note: Offered choice, but the alternatives differ only in an infra item (REF-BM-I01 multi-user), excluded from the coverage denominator and orthogonal to reference functional items; single-user matches the reference's single-user scope. Recorded as conforming; not a functional-requirement select opportunity. Tech-stack choices (SQLite, no framework) in R2 are likewise orthogonal implementation preferences and excluded.
